target: Cyn dechrau, darllenwch y cyfarwyddiadau.
english: Before starting, read the instructions.
tip: ‘cyn' plus a verb-noun means before doing something: ‘cyn dechrau' = before starting, with no word for who does it.

target: Mae'r tŷ'n cael ei baentio.
english: The house is being painted.
tip: One passive is ‘cael ei' plus a soft-mutated verb: ‘paentio' becomes ‘ei baentio', so the house is being painted.

target: Mae'r gath o dan y bwrdd.
english: The cat is under the table.
tip: Feminine nouns usually soften after ‘y' (the): ‘cath' becomes ‘y gath', while masculine ‘bwrdd' stays as ‘y bwrdd'.

target: Mae peswch arna i ers wythnos.
english: I've had a cough for a week.
tip: Welsh puts illnesses on you with ‘ar': ‘mae peswch arna i' is literally a cough is on me, not I have a cough.

target: Bydd y neges yn cael ei hanfon.
english: The message will be sent.
tip: The feminine ‘ei' (its/her) adds h to a verb starting with a vowel: ‘anfon' becomes ‘ei hanfon' here.

target: Caiff y gwaith ei wneud yn fuan.
english: The work will be done soon.
tip: ‘caiff' plus ‘ei' plus a soft-mutated verb is a passive: ‘caiff y gwaith ei wneud' = the work will be done.

target: Ar ôl i fi orffen, af i adref.
english: After I finish, I'll go home.
tip: ‘ar ôl i' plus a person plus a softened verb means after someone does: ‘ar ôl i fi orffen' = after I finish.

target: Dyn ni'n byw yn y dref ers blwyddyn.
english: We've been living in town for a year.
tip: With ‘ers', a present-tense verb means have been doing: ‘dyn ni'n byw yn y dref ers blwyddyn' = we have been living for a year.

target: Pe bai'r siop ar agor, byddwn i'n prynu bara.
english: If the shop were open, I'd buy some bread.
tip: ‘pe bai' sets up an unreal if: ‘pe bai'r siop ar agor' = if the shop were open, matched by ‘byddwn i', I would.

target: Mae angen atgyweirio'r car.
english: The car needs to be repaired.
tip: ‘mae angen' plus a verb-noun means something needs doing: ‘mae angen atgyweirio'r car' = the car needs repairing.

target: Mae gen i focs bwyd.
english: I have a lunchbox.
tip: ‘mae gen i' means I have, and the thing owned softens: ‘bocs' becomes ‘focs' in ‘mae gen i focs bwyd'.

target: Agorwyd yr amgueddfa yn 2005.
english: The museum was opened in 2005.
tip: The ending -wyd makes a past passive with no named doer: ‘agorwyd yr amgueddfa' = the museum was opened.

target: Agorwyd yr amgueddfa gan y Frenhines.
english: The museum was opened by the Queen.
tip: In a passive, ‘gan' marks who did it (by): ‘agorwyd yr amgueddfa gan y Frenhines' = opened by the Queen.

target: Darllenais i ddwy nofel yn ystod y gwyliau.
english: I read two novels during the holidays.
tip: Two has a feminine form ‘dwy' (masculine ‘dau'), used with feminine nouns: ‘ddwy nofel' = two novels.

target: Y llyfr a ddarllenais neithiwr oedd nofel dditectif.
english: The book I read last night was a detective novel.
tip: The relative ‘a' (that/which) softens the following verb: ‘darllenais' becomes ‘y llyfr a ddarllenais', the book that I read.

target: Felly, rhaid i ni weithredu'n gyflym cyn i'r sefyllfa waethygu.
english: Therefore, we must act quickly before the situation gets any worse.
tip: ‘rhaid i' plus a person plus a softened verb means must: ‘rhaid i ni weithredu' = we must act (‘gweithredu' to ‘weithredu').

target: Cafodd y gêm bêl-droed ei chanslo oherwydd glaw trwm a llifogydd ar y cae.
english: The football game was cancelled because of heavy rain and flooding on the pitch.
tip: The feminine ‘ei' changes c to ch: ‘canslo' becomes ‘ei chanslo', so ‘y gêm' was cancelled.

target: Paratowch ar gyfer yfory.
english: Prepare for tomorrow.
tip: The -wch ending makes a plural or polite command: ‘paratowch' means prepare (you).

target: Mae'r ffordd yn cael ei thrwsio.
english: The road is being repaired.
tip: Welsh forms a passive with ‘cael ei' plus a verb-noun: ‘cael ei thrwsio' means is being repaired.

target: Gwnaed y penderfyniad yn y cyfarfod.
english: The decision was made at the meeting.
tip: ‘gwnaed' is the irregular impersonal past of ‘gwneud' (do or make): ‘gwnaed y penderfyniad' means the decision was made.

target: Ymwelodd hi â'i mam-gu ddydd Sul diwethaf.
english: She visited her grandmother last Sunday.
tip: The verb ‘ymweld' takes ‘â' for what is visited: ‘ymwelodd hi â'i mam-gu' means she visited her grandmother.

target: Ganwyd fi ar y pedwerydd o Ebrill.
english: I was born on the fourth of April.
tip: Dates use an ordinal with ‘o' for of: ‘y pedwerydd o Ebrill' means the fourth of April.

target: Mae'r ŵyl wedi cael ei chynnal yma ers dros hanner can mlynedd.
english: The festival has been taking place here for over fifty years.
tip: After the feminine ‘ei' (its), c, p and t take the aspirate mutation, so ‘cynnal' becomes ‘ei chynnal' here.

target: Fe'i penodwyd i'r swydd.
english: He was appointed to the post.
tip: ‘fe'i' is the particle ‘fe' plus the object pronoun ‘i' (him or her): ‘fe'i penodwyd' means he was appointed.

target: Fe'i derbyniwyd i'r brifysgol.
english: She was accepted to the university.
tip: Feminine nouns usually soft-mutate after the article ‘yr' or ‘'r': ‘prifysgol' becomes ‘i'r brifysgol' here.

target: Mae teithio'n ehangu eich persbectif.
english: Travelling broadens your perspective.
tip: A verb-noun can act as a subject like an -ing noun: ‘mae teithio'n ehangu' means travelling broadens.

target: Sefydlwyd yr ysgol ym 1890.
english: The school was founded in 1890.
tip: The -wyd ending is the impersonal past, a passive with no named doer: ‘sefydlwyd yr ysgol' means the school was founded.

target: Ysgrifennwyd y Gododdin gan Aneirin.
english: The Gododdin was written by Aneirin.
tip: To name the doer after an impersonal verb, add ‘gan' (by): ‘gan Aneirin' means by Aneirin.

target: Mae angen gweithredu ar newid hinsawdd.
english: Action on climate change is needed.
tip: Welsh has no plain verb to need. ‘mae angen' plus a verb-noun does it: ‘mae angen gweithredu' means action is needed.

target: Mae'r myfyrwyr yn astudio yn y llyfrgell.
english: The students study in the library.
tip: ‘mae' plus ‘yn' plus a verb-noun is the present tense: ‘mae'r myfyrwyr yn astudio' means the students study.
